title: Apple Cobbler
subtitle: Soft, drop-scone biscuit topping on cinnamon-spiced baked apples
excerpt: A deep dish of Bramley apples spiced with cinnamon and lemon, topped with soft, dropped scone batter and baked until the topping is golden and the fruit is completely tender.
sourceNotes: An American dessert, now established in the British home kitchen. The British version typically uses Bramley cooking apples, which break down more completely than dessert apples, and a softer, scone-style dropped topping rather than the biscuit-style used in the southern United States.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The apple filling can be made up to 1 day ahead and refrigerated. Add the topping just before baking.

content.text: Apple cobbler is a deep-dish baked fruit pudding with a soft, pillowy dropped-scone topping rather than a pastry lid. The topping is dropped onto the fruit in rough spoonfuls and bakes into golden, irregular mounds that are crisp at the surface and soft inside. Bramley apples break down to a sharp, collapsing filling beneath, the contrast with the sweet topping is the point. Bake at 190°C for 35 to 40 minutes.

Note: this recipe uses about 700g cooking apples (Bramley). Peel, core, and slice them before starting. The ingredient list below does not include the apples as the slug may need verifying in the ingredient database, use whatever cooking apple slug is confirmed.

Preheat the oven to 190°C. Peel, core, and slice about 700g Bramley apples into 1cm slices. Toss with the caster sugar, cinnamon, lemon zest, and lemon juice in a large bowl until evenly coated. Tip into a 1.5-litre baking dish. Dot the butter over the surface.

Combine the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Add the cold butter cubes and rub into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs. Whisk the milk and egg together, then stir into the flour mixture until just combined, the batter will be thick and a little rough. Do not over-mix: a few streaks of flour are fine.

Drop large spoonfuls of the cobbler batter over the apples, leaving gaps so the steam can escape and some fruit shows through. Scatter with demerara sugar. Bake at 190°C for 35 to 40 minutes until the topping is deep golden and a skewer inserted in the topping comes out clean. The fruit should be completely soft and bubbling at the edges. Leave to settle for 5 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: The topping is raw in the middle but brown on top
items.cause: The topping was spread too thick in the centre, or the oven temperature was too high.
items.fix: Drop the topping in thinner spoonfuls, leaving more fruit exposed. Tent with foil if it is browning before cooking through.

items.symptom: The apples are watery and the cobbler is sitting in juice
items.cause: Very juicy apples, or the cobbler was not baked for long enough.
items.fix: Toss the sliced apples with 1 teaspoon of cornflour before adding to the dish. Continue baking until the juices at the edges are thickened and bubbling.

items.symptom: The topping is tough rather than tender
items.cause: The batter was over-mixed, developing the gluten in the flour.
items.fix: Mix only until the wet and dry ingredients just come together. Lumpy batter is correct for cobbler.

content.text: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days, covered. Reheat in the oven at 180°C for 15 minutes until hot through. The topping softens in storage but regains some crispness in the oven.
